## Installation

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("IMPALA-Consortium/gsm.ctas")
```

```{r load, message = FALSE}
library(gsm.ctas)
library(dplyr)
```

## The shape of the pipeline


## Input data

`pharmaversesdtm` provides the SDTM domains. The example is cut down to six
sites and a handful of tests to keep the engine fast.

```{r data}

dfDM <- pharmaversesdtm::dm
dfVS <- pharmaversesdtm::vs
dfLB <- pharmaversesdtm::lb
dfRS <- pharmaversesdtm::rs_onco

lRaw <- list(
  Raw_DM = as.data.frame(dfDM),
  Raw_VS = as.data.frame(dfVS),
  Raw_LB = as.data.frame(dfLB),
  Raw_RS = as.data.frame(dfRS)
)
```

## 1. Mapping

```{r mappings}
lMappingWorkflows <- workr::MakeWorkflowList(
  strNames = NULL,
  strPath = system.file("workflow/1_mappings", package = "gsm.ctas"),
  strPackage = NULL
)

lIngest <- gsm.mapping::Ingest(
  lRaw, gsm.mapping::CombineSpecs(lMappingWorkflows)
)

lMapped <- suppressWarnings(
  gsm.core::RunWorkflows(lWorkflows = lMappingWorkflows, lData = lIngest)
)

str(lMapped)
```


## 2.1 Data Types / Metrics

`Standardize_Domain()` renames an SDTM domain into the CTAS vocabulary and,
by default, emits a numeric-ready frame that can flow straight into
`Analyze_CTAS()`. Range, missing-ratio and categorical metrics chain an
`Input_*()` transform in between to overwrite `result` and
`parameter_category_3`.

### Range-normalized labs

`Input_Range()` rescales each result into its reference range; values with
missing bounds are dropped.

```{r range}
as_tibble(lMapped$Mapped_LB)

dfStandard <- Standardize_Domain(
  dfDomain = lMapped$Mapped_LB,
  dfSubjects = lMapped$Mapped_Subjects,
  strTestCDCol = "LBTESTCD",
  strTestCol = "LBTEST",
  strValueCol = "LBSTRESN",
  strLowCol = "LBSTNRLO",
  strHighCol = "LBSTNRHI",
  strCategory = "Labs",
  strExcludePattern = NULL
)

as_tibble(dfStandard)

dfRange <- Input_Range(dfStandard)

as_tibble(dfRange)

dfAna <- Analyze_CTAS(dfRange)

as_tibble(dfAna)
```

### Numeric vital signs

`Standardize_Domain()` stamps `parameter_category_3 = "numeric"` and
`result = as.numeric(value)`, so no separate transform step is needed.

```{r numeric}
as_tibble(lMapped$Mapped_VS)

dfStandard <- Standardize_Domain(
  dfDomain = lMapped$Mapped_VS,
  dfSubjects = lMapped$Mapped_Subjects,
  strTestCDCol = "VSTESTCD",
  strTestCol = "VSTEST",
  strValueCol = "VSSTRESN",
  strCategory = "Vital Signs",
  strExcludePattern = NULL
)

as_tibble(dfStandard)

dfAna <- Analyze_CTAS(dfStandard)

as_tibble(dfAna)
```

### Ratio-missing labs

`Input_Missing()` converts each observation into a 0/1 indicator of whether
the value is missing, so the resulting CTAS signal is per-site missingness
over time.

```{r ratio_missing}
dfStandard <- Standardize_Domain(
  dfDomain = lMapped$Mapped_LB,
  dfSubjects = lMapped$Mapped_Subjects,
  strTestCDCol = "LBTESTCD",
  strTestCol = "LBTEST",
  strValueCol = "LBSTRESN",
  strCategory = "Labs",
  strExcludePattern = NULL
)

as_tibble(dfStandard)

dfMissing <- Input_Missing(dfStandard)

as_tibble(dfMissing)

dfAna <- Analyze_CTAS(dfMissing)

as_tibble(dfAna)
```

### Categorical response

`Input_OneHot()` expands a categorical variable such as SDTM RS `RSSTRESC`
into one binary CTAS timeseries per observed level, so `Analyze_CTAS()` can
flag sites whose per-level rates drift from their peers.

```{r categorical}
dfRS <- pharmaversesdtm::rs_onco
dfRS <- dfRS[dfRS$RSTESTCD == "OVRLRESP", ]

dfStandard <- Standardize_Domain(
  dfDomain = dfRS,
  dfSubjects = lMapped$Mapped_Subjects,
  strTestCDCol = "RSTESTCD",
  strTestCol = "RSTEST",
  strValueCol = "RSSTRESC",
  strCategory = "Disease Response",
  strExcludePattern = NULL
)

as_tibble(dfStandard)

dfOneHot <- Input_OneHot(dfStandard)

as_tibble(dfOneHot)

unique(dfOneHot$parameter_id)

dfAna <- Analyze_CTAS(dfOneHot)

as_tibble(dfAna)
```

### Stitching metrics on the same field

ctasapp groups sidebar entries by `parameter_category_2`, so when the same
LB test flows through both `Input_Range()` and `Input_Missing()` the two
metrics collapse into a single field entry with a faceted plot.
`Standardize_Domain()` sets `parameter_category_2` to the raw test code
(e.g. `"ALT"`); the `Input_*()` wrappers only prefix `parameter_id` itself
(`RANGE_ALT`, `MISS_ALT`) so the score tables stay unique.

```{r stitching}
dfLB <- Standardize_Domain(
  dfDomain = lMapped$Mapped_LB,
  dfSubjects = lMapped$Mapped_Subjects,
  strTestCDCol = "LBTESTCD",
  strTestCol = "LBTEST",
  strValueCol = "LBSTRESN",
  strLowCol = "LBSTNRLO",
  strHighCol = "LBSTNRHI",
  strCategory = "Labs",
  strExcludePattern = NULL
)

intersect(
  unique(Input_Range(dfLB)$parameter_category_2),
  unique(Input_Missing(dfLB)$parameter_category_2)
) |> head()
```



## 2. Metrics

```{r metrics}
lMetricWorkflows <- workr::MakeWorkflowList(
  strNames = NULL,
  strPath = system.file("workflow/2_metrics", package = "gsm.ctas"),
  strPackage = NULL
)

lAnalysis <- suppressWarnings(
  gsm.core::RunWorkflows(lWorkflows = lMetricWorkflows, lData = lMapped)
)

str(lAnalysis)
```

Feature selection is one boolean per CTAS feature in `meta:`, so any metric
can toggle features individually:

```yaml
meta:
  ID: numeric
  FeatureAutocorr: true
  FeatureAverage: true
  FeatureSD: true
  FeatureRange: false
  FeatureUniqueValueCountRelative: true
  FeatureOwnSiteSimilScore: false
  FeatureLOF: false
```

Multi-study is honoured automatically: when `Mapped_Subjects` contains several
values in `studyid`, `Analyze_CTAS()` splits the input by study, runs CTAS on
each, and stacks the results with a `study` column tagged onto every row.

## 3. Reporting: writing ctasapp shards

`Bind_Analysis()` concatenates one named shard (`"results"`, `"input"` or
`"untransformed"`) across every metric workflow output; `Results.yaml`
wraps three of those steps into a single reporting call and packages the
three bound frames as a list ready to be handed to
[ctasapp](https://github.com/IMPALA-Consortium/ctasapp) validators or
written to parquet.

```{r reporting_results, eval = FALSE}
lReportingWorkflows <- workr::MakeWorkflowList(
  strNames = NULL,
  strPath = system.file("workflow/3_reporting", package = "gsm.ctas"),
  strPackage = NULL
)

lReporting <- gsm.core::RunWorkflows(
  lWorkflows = lReportingWorkflows["Results"],
  lData = list(lAnalyzed = lAnalysis)
)

str(lReporting$Reporting_Results)
```

`Write_Results()` is the one-shot alternative that binds and writes to
disk. Parquet is the default because `input` grows quickly.

```{r reporting, eval = FALSE}
Write_Results(lReporting, strDir = "pub", strFormat = "parquet")
```

Point [ctasapp](https://github.com/IMPALA-Consortium/ctasapp) at the same
`pub/` folder by copying the shipped `ctasapp.yml` next to `app.R` and
setting its `embedded:` block to the parquet files written above.
`run_ctas_app()` discovers the config in the current working directory and
loads the embedded dataset through the same validation pipeline it uses
for uploads.

```{r ctasapp, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("IMPALA-Consortium/ctasapp")

file.copy(
  system.file("ctasapp.yml", package = "ctasapp"),
  "ctasapp.yml",
  overwrite = TRUE
)

# Edit ctasapp.yml so the embedded block points at pub/:
#
# embedded:
#   results: pub/results.parquet
#   input: pub/input.parquet
#   untransformed: pub/untransformed.parquet  # optional

ctasapp::run_ctas_app()
```
